summary: Defines Connectivity Verification types that use Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) together with Virtual Circuit Connectivity Verification (VCCV). VCCV gives a pseudowire a control channel for operations and management checks, and BFD is used over that channel to verify the connection is alive.

eli5.summary: A pseudowire is like a pretend wire running through a network. This document adds a quick way for both ends to check that the pretend wire is still working.

subtitle: Four ways to run BFD fault detection over a pseudowire's VCCV control channel.

tldr.problem: A pseudowire needs a quick way for both ends to detect data-plane failures, and sometimes to pass fault status along, using the VCCV control channel.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines four BFD Connectivity Verification types, two encapsulations (with or without IP/UDP headers) crossed with two functions (fault detection only, or detection plus status signaling). BFD runs in asynchronous mode, one session per pseudowire.
tldr.outcome: Both ends pick one common type using a fixed precedence and keep it until the pseudowire is re-signaled. Later RFCs have updated this document.

sections.title: BFD over the VCCV Control Channel
sections.content:
Virtual Circuit Connectivity Verification (VCCV) gives a pseudowire (PW) a control channel plus management functions such as connectivity verification. This RFC defines new Connectivity Verification (CV) Types that use Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) as the VCCV payload.

BFD is used mainly to detect data-plane failures on the pseudowire. Some of the BFD CV Types can also carry fault status between the endpoints, which can be translated into the native OAM status codes of access technologies such as ATM, Frame Relay or Ethernet. The details of that interworking are out of scope here.

The CV Types do not depend on the PW demultiplexer, so they apply to both MPLS and L2TPv3 pseudowires. The document covers single-segment pseudowires only, and only BFD asynchronous mode.
sections.eli5: Two friends hold the ends of a long string and tug it now and then. If the tugs stop, one knows the string broke. BFD does that for a pseudowire.

sections.title: The Four BFD CV Types
sections.content:
Four CV Types are defined. They combine two encapsulations with two functions. The CV Type is a bitmask, so several can be advertised at once, but only one is used.

  • 0x04: BFD with IP/UDP headers, fault detection only.
  • 0x08: BFD with IP/UDP headers, fault detection and AC/PW fault status signaling.
  • 0x10: BFD in the PW Associated Channel Header (PW-ACH), without IP/UDP headers, fault detection only.
  • 0x20: BFD in the PW-ACH, without IP/UDP headers, fault detection and status signaling.

The same values are registered for MPLS and L2TPv3 pseudowires.
sections.eli5: There are four kinds of hello message: two ways of wrapping them, and two jobs. One job is just "are you there?" and the other also tells what is wrong.

sections.title: How BFD Runs on a Pseudowire
sections.content:
Both ends must agree on the BFD CV Type. On statically provisioned pseudowires, both are configured with the same type. On dynamic ones, both must have signaled the control channel and the ability to run BFD on it.

Once a type is chosen, each node sends BFD Control packets on the VCCV control channel. Discriminators are not exchanged. The PW demultiplexer, such as the MPLS PW label or L2TPv3 session ID, provides the context to bind the session, so single-hop BFD initialization applies. There is one BFD session per pseudowire. Both endpoints are Active and send initial packets with a Your Discriminator of zero. BFD MUST run in asynchronous mode, and both endpoints MUST send BFD messages, so the operation is symmetrical.

The RFC gives an example. If the downstream PE stops receiving BFD Control messages for the number of intervals set by Detect Mult, it declares the PW down in its receive direction. It signals state Down with Diagnostic code 1 (Control Detection Time Expired). The upstream PE then marks the PW down in its transmit direction, sending Down with Diagnostic code 3 (Neighbor signaled session down). How the attachment circuits are told is left to another document.
sections.eli5: Each end keeps saying "I'm here" at regular beats. If one end misses too many beats, it says "I can't hear you", and the other end then knows the wire is broken in its direction too.

sections.title: The Two Encapsulations
sections.content:
With IP/UDP encapsulation, BFD Control packets travel in UDP with destination port 3784 and a source port from 49152 through 65535. The IP version must match the one used for signaling, or be configured for static pseudowires. The destination address is chosen from 127/8 for IPv4, or from 0:0:0:0:0:FFFF:127.0.0.0/104 for IPv6, and TTL or Hop Limit is 255 under the GTSM procedures. If a PW-ACH is used, its Channel Type MUST indicate IPv4 (0x0021) or IPv6 (0x0057). This encapsulation allows other IP-based VCCV types, such as ICMP Ping or LSP Ping, to be used at the same time.

With PW-ACH encapsulation, a raw BFD Control packet follows the PW Associated Channel Header directly, with no IP/UDP headers. The pseudowire MUST use the PW-ACH control word format, and the Channel Type MUST be 0x0007, "BFD Control, PW-ACH-encapsulated". Pseudowires that do not use a control word or L2-specific sublayer with the PW-ACH MUST NOT use types 0x10 or 0x20.
sections.eli5: You can send the hello inside a full envelope with a postal address, or hand it over inside a special pouch that only this tunnel understands. The pouch needs a pouch-shaped tunnel.

sections.title: Choosing a CV Type
sections.content:
Because BFD is bidirectional, only CV Types that were both advertised and received can be selected, and only one type is used. If several are in common, the one highest on this list wins: 0x20, then 0x10, then 0x08, then 0x04. The general precedence rules for CC and CV Types are in RFC 5085.

Other rules apply as well:

  • Types 0x08 and 0x20 SHOULD NOT be used when a control protocol such as LDP or L2TPv3 can already signal AC/PW status.
  • Types 0x04 and 0x10 can be used with or without such a protocol. Fault status is then conveyed by other means, such as LDP status messages or the Circuit Status AVP in L2TPv3.
  • Once chosen, a type MUST be used until the pseudowire is re-signaled. Changing it means tearing down and re-establishing the pseudowire.
sections.eli5: Both ends show which kinds of hello they can use. They pick the best kind they have in common from a fixed list, and stick with it until they start over.

sections.title: Congestion Considerations
sections.content:
BFD uses a desired minimum transmit interval and a required minimum receive interval, and its packets have a fixed size. Its bandwidth is therefore limited by configuration. As in RFC 5085, that is enough protection against congestion as long as BFD's configured maximum bit-rate is minimal compared to the pseudowire's. If that cannot be guaranteed, BFD will be required to use an adaptive congestion control mechanism.

The VCCV channel MUST NOT be rate-limited below the maximum configurable BFD bandwidth, or BFD will not work correctly. It SHOULD NOT add a congestion control loop that interferes with BFD's.
sections.eli5: Hello messages are small and sent at a set pace, so they hardly crowd the wire. If the wire is small, the pace must slow down.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Routers that implement these CV Types are subject to the security considerations of RFC 5085, RFC 5880 and RFC 5881, and the RFC says it raises no additional issues. IP/UDP-encapsulated BFD uses the TTL and Hop Limit procedures of RFC 5881, including the Generalized TTL Security Mechanism (GTSM), as a security mechanism.
sections.eli5: Hellos that come from too far away are thrown out because their travel counter is wrong, so strangers cannot easily fake them.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA added the four bit values (0x04, 0x08, 0x10, 0x20) to the MPLS "VCCV Connectivity Verification (CV) Types" registry, and the same four to the L2TPv3 VCCV Capability AVP (Attribute Type 96) values. It also reserved the new Pseudowire Associated Channel Type 0x0007, "BFD Control, PW-ACH encapsulation (without IP/UDP Headers)".
sections.eli5: The official lists of numbers got new entries so everyone uses the same numbers for these four kinds of hello.
